_meta.method: 4-member council (rigorous/opus, pragmatist/sonnet, contrarian/default model after fable was unavailable, plain-language/haiku); anonymised peer review; chairman score = member scores weighted by (5 - average peer rank).
chairman_corrections: Gulshan and Apcotex both show TTM PAT Rs 170.7 Cr: verified as a coincidence (each equals mcap / provider P/E: 1,022/6.0 and 2,509/14.7), not a transcription error.
Jeena Sikho memo phrase 'debt-free' conflicts with reported D/E 0.33 (likely lease liabilities); flagged.
CFO/PAT mixes periods (latest-FY CFO over TTM PAT) for several names; treat as indicative.

member_reasons.plain: Makes silver-based electrical contacts. The sentence is simple, but much of the profit jump came from silver price gains, which may reverse. Hard to call that a repeatable business.
member_reasons.contrarian: A 49% ROCE and 15.6x are measured on silver-inflated FY26 profit (+194%), so 'normalised' is not normal. A silver reversal unwinds inventory gains. The underlying switchgear-contact moat deserves a separate, ex-silver valuation.
member_reasons.rigorous: Normalising to FY26 PAT does not remove the windfall: FY26 PAT (+194%) was itself driven by silver. Hedge MTM is booked as an exceptional item, D/E is 0.69 with no CFO, and the 49% ROCE is inflated.
member_reasons.pragmatist: Profit rides on silver inventory and hedge gains, so earnings quality is hard to read. Next check: normalised margin excluding silver gains and exposure if silver reverses.
